{{Short description|British academic}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2019}}
'''Charles Smith''' (b [[Huntingdon]], 11 May 1844; d [[Cambridge]] 13 November 1916)<ref>{{cite news | title=The Master Of Sidney | newspaper=[[The Times]] | location=London, England | date=14 November 1916 | page=4 | issue=41324}}</ref> was a 20th-century British academic.<ref>Amongst others he wrote "An Elementary Treatise on Conic Sections", 1882; "An Elementary Treatise on Solid Geometry", 1884; "Elementary Algebra", 1886; "Treatise on Algebra", 1887; "Arithmetic", 1891; "Geometrical Conics" 1894; and "Euclid" 1901  > [[British Library]]  web site accessed 17:48 [[GMT]] Tuesday 31 July 2018</ref>

Smith was educated at [[Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{Who's Who | title=Smith, Charles | id = U195346 | type = was | volume = 1920–2016 | edition = July2018 online | access-date = 31 July 2018 }}</ref> He became a [[Fellow]] of [[Sidney Sussex]] in 1868; [[Tutor]] in 1875; and [[Master (college)|Master]] in 1890. He was [[List of Vice-Chancellors of the University of Cambridge|Vice-Chancellor of the University of Cambridge]] from 1895 to 1897.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.v-c.admin.cam.ac.uk/role-vice-chancellor/history-vice-chancellorship | title=Vice-Chancellor's Office | publisher=University of Cambridge | accessdate=30 September 2019 }}</ref>
